newsitem.title: CHINA: China says regrets Denmark plan on rights censure.
newsitem.headline: China says regrets Denmark plan on rights censure.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it regretted Denmark's decision to press ahead with U.N. criticism of its human rights policies and that relations would be affected.
But it stopped short of saying that ties would be hurt with all countries that supported the resolution, expected to be raised by Denmark at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva.
"We express our regret over the Danish government's decision to take the lead in putting forward this anti-China resolution," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told reporters.
Denmark vowed on Monday to press ahead with a U.N. resolution criticising China's human rights record, defying Beijing's warning that the move would severely damage ties.
"If certain countries seek to lead such anti-China resolutions, naturally there will be some effect on relations and normal exchanges in the human rights area," Shen said.
Asked whether other supporters of the resolution would face similar harm to ties, Shen said merely that this would not be in the interest of the two sides.

Assured of the backing of the United States and other European Union states, with the notable exceptions of France and Germany, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said his country would present the resolution in Geneva this week.

Previous attempts to condemn China on human rights in a U.N. resolution following Beijing's bloody 1989 crackdown on pro-democracy protesters have failed. China has rallied enough support each year to block the move.

President Jiang Zemin told visiting French Defence Minister Charles Millon on Monday he hoped France would play a role in persuading more Western countries to avoid confrontation in favour of dialogue.
China's Jiang said differing views on human rights were normal and inevitable among different countries with different social systems, cultural traditions and historical backgrounds.
